summary: FamilySearch-only claimed father of Stephen Scott - unsupported.
bio:
A FamilySearch profile gives Stephen Scott's father as Daniel Scott 1788-1811. Flagged as speculative/do not copy.

A 'Daniel Scott Jr.' headed a household in Pittston Township in 1810: a man aged 26-44, a woman aged 16-25 and three young children, two of them boys ([R4-S1]). The man's age fits the tree's birth year of 1778 (and rules out FamilySearch's 1788, since he would then have been 22), and the young wife fits Hannah Devens (b. 1787). The 'Jr.' implies an older Daniel Scott in the same area; a Daniel Scott appears among the 1796 taxables of neighbouring Providence Township ([R4-S2]). A Joseph Scott and a Stephen Scott (aged 16-25) were enumerated on the same Pittston page ([R4-S1]). This is consistent with, but does not prove, the FamilySearch claim that Daniel and Hannah (Devens) Scott were the parents of Stephen J. Scott (b. Feb 1806). The FamilySearch profile makes him a son of Matthew Scott of Bennington, Vermont (d. 1789); the 'Jr.' in 1810 sits awkwardly with that, unless 'Jr.' distinguished him from an unrelated older Daniel.
sources: [R4-S1] 1810 US census, Pittstown [Pittston] Twp, Luzerne Co., PA, p.656 (FS index ark 1:1:XH2B-VYH) (primary) https://ancestors.familysearch.org/service/tree/tree-data/published/sources/GC9K-HF1/images/i/0/image.jpg
[R4-S2] Pearce, Annals of Luzerne County (1866), list of taxables in Providence Township in 1796 (includes Daniel Scott) (secondary) https://archive.org/details/annalsofluzernec01pear
